name: VEA
summary: AI built for entrepreneurs, not enterprises: VEA learns your business like a great employee would, finds the constraint keeping you stuck, and helps you solve it — then finds the next one.
best_for: hands-on entrepreneurs and small-business owners buried in operational detail who want AI that learns their specific business and helps surface what's actually holding it back — explicitly not enterprise software
skip_if: you run a larger organization with established teams and processes (VEA itself positions against that), or you need a task-specific tool rather than a business-level advisor
honest_knock: The pitch is unusually bold: an AI that learns your business the way a great employee would, finds the constraint keeping you stuck, and helps you solve it. That ambition is also the honest caveat — it's a young product making a big promise, its price ladder was rebuilt in August 2026 with a top tier at $597 per user a month, and independent review coverage is still thin (one rating on the US App Store on 29 September 2026). Judge it in the 7-day trial on one measurable question: did it identify a constraint you recognize as painfully real? If yes, it earns the next month. If its advice stays generic — the thing its own positioning promises to avoid — walk.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-29 on the pricing section of VEA's own site, vea.ai; amounts unchanged since 2026-09-02) Four tiers, per user per month, monthly against annual: Business Class $30 / $25, First Class $50 / $40, Private Jet $150 / $120 and Owners Club $597 / $497. The three-tier ladder we read in August ($31.95 / $24.95, $49.95 / $39.95, $77.95 / $59.95) was replaced between our 2 August and 1 September 2026 captures. Every tier now carries a 7-day free trial ('Try VEA free for 7 days before your first payment'), and the old 'Starting at $24.95' marketing line is gone. Annual billing saves roughly 17% to 20%. The page separates the tiers by scope rather than seat count: Business Class gives AI assistants for accounting, assets, checklists, customers, services, tasks and tickets; First Class adds a company knowledge base, an AI resume analyser for recruitment, a checklist builder and team visibility; Private Jet adds 'most advanced AI models'; Owners Club adds an AI mentor, an executive assistant, a daily brief and a private owner's knowledge base, sold with the line 'doubles your revenue in 12 months. Guaranteed.', for which the pricing section gives no terms.
